column1: # Fuzz-coverage exemptions — the ERROR TERM of `zig build check-fuzz`, not its
# mechanism. Read `checkFuzz` in build.zig first; it explains why obligation is
# derived (ANCHORS.tsv CLASS A/B  AND  a `pub fn` that accepts caller-supplied
# bytes) rather than declared, and this file only holds the cases where that
# derivation is true but the bytes are ours.
# The gate refuses a row that is not doing real work. All five rules are checked
# against the tree on every run (see `checkFuzzExempt`):
#   1. REASON is EMIT-ONLY or PRE-PARSED. Nothing else. No free prose.
#   2. The module exists in build.zig's module_list.
#   3. The gate would otherwise have flagged the module — CLASS A/B *and* a
#      byte-accepting public API. A pre-emptive exemption is an error.
#   4. The module has NO `testing.fuzz(` harness. The day someone fuzzes it, the
#      row becomes a lie and the build says so.
#   5. PRE-PARSED must name a sibling that is a declared dep of this module AND
#      is itself fuzzed. EMIT-ONLY must still state the argument in EVIDENCE.
# If this file grows past a handful of rows, the derivation is wrong and should

column3: Produces the Prometheus text exposition format; it never parses it. Its three byte-accepting public functions (Registry.counter/gauge/histogram) take metric NAME, HELP and label strings that our own callers author in Zig source — there is no path from a socket to any of them. The router middleware it ships observes already-parsed http.Request values. Overturn this row the moment a scrape PARSER lands.
